Are any of the new closure lemmas stated with unnecessarily strong typeclass assumptions or overly specialized types (e.g. restricting to `𝕜 → 𝕜` for mul/div/pow/zpow) when existing `MeromorphicAt` lemmas support more general codomains?

comprehension.summary: Introduces a global predicate `Meromorphic` (meromorphic at every point) as a shorthand for `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ`, and adds a basic closure API (neg/add/sub/mul/div/pow/zpow/deriv and finite sum/product) with `fun_prop`/simp lemmas to support automation.

proposed_edit.new_declaration:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_add (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (fun x ↦ f x + g x) := by
  -- reuse the `MeromorphicOn` lemma on `Set.univ`
  have hf' : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ := by
    intro x hx; simpa [Meromorphic] using hf x
  have hg' : MeromorphicOn g Set.univ := by
    intro x hx; simpa [Meromorphic] using hg x
  simpa [Meromorphic, meromorphicOn_univ] using
    (MeromorphicOn.fun_add (U := Set.univ) (f := f) (g := g) hf' hg')

candidates.requested_change: Replace the proof of `Meromorphic.fun_add` with one that reuses the existing lemma `MeromorphicOn.fun_add` on `Set.univ` (instead of reproving pointwise via `MeromorphicAt.add`).

lemma meromorphicOn_univ {f : 𝕜 → E} : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f := by
